Hi ya Revivalfx, Astro..

I’m no expert but if it was me I would treat it as a QM.. What I’m starting to realize with chart time is not to be too rigid with the shape and size of these PA patterns but most importantly is to distinguish between good and bad patterns in good areas on the chart.. don't just take any pattern blindly with out any criteria behind it which will come with chart time..

Another thing you will see with chart time is that these patterns are all very similar in their own way or are part of another pattern be it a QM, H&S, WE, Can Can, Compression..

Cheers, Adrian

Thanks for your ideas. just wondering what's the best way to spot QM's

1. Find strong S/D areas HTF and then drop down to LTF charts to look for QM setups or 2. pick a timeframe/s and once QM setup occurs look for HTF confirmation to validate the setup.

Would like to hear some opinions on this.

astro wrote: Thanks for your ideas. just wondering what's the best way to spot QM's

1. Find strong S/D areas HTF and then drop down to LTF charts to look for QM setups or 2. pick a timeframe/s and once QM setup occurs look for HTF confirmation to validate the setup.

Would like to hear some opinions on this.

I usually mark up the higher TF areas and then wait till price approaches the area then drop down 1 or 2 TF’s to see what PA occurs there be it a QM, CanCan, Compression, etc..

If you see a QM on a higher TF then I would look at dropping down to a lower TF and seeing if you have another PA pattern again just for a tighter entry and stop placement..or you could just place a limit order in there for a TT if you are confident in your set up..
